review_basis: registered FDMA static-electricity and incident-prevention source bindings

decisions.rationale: Source-specific gasoline-vapor ignition mechanism is distinct and relevant.
Static ignition likelihood is a separate causal proposition from C001.
Static-removal display requirement is source-explicit.
Engine-off fueling is a distinct operational prevention rule.
Open-flame prohibition tests direct ignition-source control.
Container-injection prohibition is a separate handling control.
Closing vehicle doors/windows is a specific pre-fueling instruction.
Touching vehicle metal operationalizes the static-removal rule rather than repeating signage wording.
One-person fueling is a separate user-behavior control.
Keeping children away from the filler area is a distinct proximity control.
Ventilation-failure → vapor-accumulation → ignition is a high-value incident pathway.
Filter blockage/switch omission concretizes ventilation-maintenance failure.
Equipment grounding/static eliminators are distinct engineering controls.
Personnel static-control clothing/tools are distinct from equipment controls.
Oily-deposit housekeeping risk is an independent combustible-management pathway.
Explosion-proof equipment directly addresses electrical ignition in vapor areas.
Bare flame, repair sparks and electrical sparks define a distinct ignition-source-management scope.
Hose/nozzle static control applies grounding to transfer-line flow, distinct from paint-equipment control.
Automatic stop plus procedure/inventory control addresses overfill, not ignition alone.
Cleaning/washing/ventilation before hot work is a distinct residual-vapor decision boundary.

collision_review.note: All 20 accepted B9 questions test materially different safety controls, causal paths, or operational contexts; none duplicates canonical 111.

source_review_scope: Final canonical source verification remains separate after integration.
